- Foreign students who earn an associate degree or higher in Taiwan can apply to extend their stay for up to two years. [1]
- During the extended stay, graduates can work without obtaining a separate work permit and their family members can also apply to remain in Taiwan. [1]
- Graduates are not subject to restrictions on the types of professional or technical jobs they can take, employer qualifications or minimum salary thresholds. [1]
- After the extended stay ends, graduates can transition to other residency programs based on a points system or regulations governing foreign professionals. [1]

- A bachelor's degree takes four years and at least 128 credits in total. [1]

- 12 extra graduation credits are required for admission on an equivalent qualification. [1]
- Military training and PE do not count toward those 12 credits. [1]
- The requirement is stated in National Central University Study Regulations, Article 48. [1]
- For more information, contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs 教務處課務組 at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw. [1]

- At least 16 credits each semester in years one to three and at least 9 credits each semester in year four. [1]
- If you take fewer credits, you must obtain approval from your advisor and department head; otherwise you can be dismissed. [1]

- International students take the full-year five-credit course “Chinese for Overseas Chinese Students” instead of the 3-credit Chinese (A) and 2-credit Chinese (B) courses. [1]
- This is specified in Article 3 of the common-course regulations, which states that overseas Chinese and international students must take the five-credit “Chinese for Overseas Chinese Students” and are not required to take “Chinese (B): Chinese Writing.” [1]
- For more details, contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs 教務處課務組 at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw. [1]

- 6 credits of Mandarin courses at the Language Center instead of freshman Chinese [1]

- Students are required to take five physical education (PE) courses in five semesters (including Freshman PE I, Freshman PE II, and three PE interest electives in the following three semesters), but any course credit earned from these five PE courses do not count towards the number of course credits required for graduation. [1]
- After the five semesters you may take a 1-credit PE course, which also does not count toward graduation. [1]
- The PE requirement is detailed in National Central University Study Regulations, Article 13. [1]
- For more information, contact the Division of Curriculum, Office of Academic Affairs 教務處課務組 at https://pdc.adm.ncu.edu.tw/p/412-1019-1763.php?Lang=zh-tw. [1]
